data: Create an original, severely abstract dark cubist mural painted as one rough, full-frame surface in only charcoal-black, chalk white, and ash gray. View the composition from above: Márton Kádár from the second image is reduced to a large fictional protagonist seated and crouched diagonally across the ground plane, preserving only his recognizable broad facial mass, short swept-back hair silhouette, and stern identity through displaced angular fragments, never a realistic face. His head bends into a contemplative pose, one hand pressed near his brow and the other close to his chest, both hands distorted into broad interlocking shapes. Surround him with swollen rounded masses, crescents, bent arcs, and sweeping bands that press, pull, and collide. Reinterpret the first image’s raised-hand gesture as a secondary abstract network figure: a small white eye-like mask containing a branching node-and-connection symbol, reacting as an observation of light through radiating chalk strokes. Fuse this figure into the surrounding network of compressed interlocking circles, wedges, and irregular member-state-like cells, suggesting political union and regulation without reproducing a map or flag. Use the first image’s eye motif only as a structural cue for the reacting network symbol, never as a pasted element. Fracture the protagonist’s face into mismatched masks and merge bodies into the terrain. Cover the entire surface with raw charcoal, scraped pigment, broken brush marks, worn plaster, and layered black-gray tonal transitions, with no text, logos, flags, or additional colors.
